title: PostgreSQL 16 Diagnostic & Catalog Inspection
description: Inspect PostgreSQL 16 server metadata, database name, connected user, and uptime parameters from pg_stat_database.
setup_sql:
-- Diagnostic metadata inspection
SELECT version(), current_database(), current_user;
query_solution: SELECT datname, numbackends, xact_commit, xact_rollback, blks_read, blks_hit FROM pg_stat_database WHERE datname = current_database();
verification_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_database WHERE datname = current_database();
notes: Queries pg_stat_database on live PostgreSQL 16 server.

title: Employee Department Ranking (DENSE_RANK)
description: Compute the salary ranking of each employee inside their department using DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC).
setup_sql:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS lab_employees (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  name VARCHAR(100),
  department VARCHAR(50),
  salary NUMERIC(10, 2)
);
INSERT INTO lab_employees (name, department, salary) VALUES
  ('Alice Johnson', 'Engineering', 95000),
  ('Bob Smith', 'Engineering', 88000),
  ('Charlie Brown', 'Engineering', 95000),
  ('Diana Prince', 'Marketing', 78000),
  ('Evan Wright', 'Marketing', 69000)
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
query_solution: SELECT name, department, salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) as dept_rank FROM lab_employees ORDER BY department, dept_rank;
notes: Demonstrates window partitioning in genuine PostgreSQL.

title: Recursive CTE: Organizational Hierarchy
description: Traverse the company management tree using WITH RECURSIVE to compute each employee's depth level from the CEO.
setup_sql:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS org_hierarchy (
  emp_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
  name VARCHAR(100),
  manager_id INT REFERENCES org_hierarchy(emp_id)
);
INSERT INTO org_hierarchy (emp_id, name, manager_id) VALUES
  (1, 'CEO Arun', NULL),
  (2, 'VP Tech Sarah', 1),
  (3, 'VP Product David', 1),
  (4, 'Staff Eng Elena', 2),
  (5, 'Senior Eng Carlos', 4)
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
query_solution:
WITH RECURSIVE OrgChart AS (
  SELECT emp_id, name, manager_id, 1 as level
  FROM org_hierarchy
  WHERE manager_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.emp_id, e.name, e.manager_id, o.level + 1
  FROM org_hierarchy e
  JOIN OrgChart o ON e.manager_id = o.emp_id
)
SELECT emp_id, name, level FROM OrgChart ORDER BY level, emp_id;

title: JSONB Indexing & Querying in PostgreSQL
description: Store and filter arbitrary payload data using PostgreSQL JSONB containment operator @>.
query_solution: SELECT event_id, payload->>'event' as event_name, payload->>'user_id' as user_id FROM customer_events WHERE payload @> '{"device": "desktop"}'::jsonb;
notes: Native JSONB indexing and query capability in PostgreSQL.
